annotationRationale: Regular-hexagon geometry determines the larger equilateral triangle and the small 30-60-90 corner triangles. Subtracting their areas gives the intersection.
sourceMethod: Followed the first official method: use trapezoid midlines to find XYZ, then subtract three congruent corner triangles. Defined both auxiliary intersections in words and supplied the angle reasoning for their dimensions.

review.mathCheck: The trapezoid midline gives \(XZ=3/2\), and rotational symmetry makes XYZ equilateral. The stated angle chase correctly gives a corner triangle with hypotenuse \(1/2\), legs \(1/4\) and \(\sqrt3/4\), and area \(\sqrt3/32\). Removing three disjoint congruent corners yields \(9\sqrt3/16-3\sqrt3/32=15\sqrt3/32\), choice C. Open boundaries do not affect area.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful rewording of the first MAA solution 24, pages 11–12, consistent with its shaded figure. It retains the trapezoid-midline and corner-subtraction approach while supplying explicit angles instead of the source's abbreviated congruence claim.
review.annotationCheck: Composite area and 30° right-triangle properties are correctly assessed. The regular-polygon, equilateral-triangle and triangle-area nodes provide relevant background. The stated midline facts make the method reconstructable.
